intro: An aggregate accuracy hides which categories a model confuses. Count actual-versus-predicted outcomes before choosing a remedy.
task: Return a multiclass confusion matrix with actual labels on rows and predicted labels on columns.
requirements: actual and predicted are nonempty same-length vectors of integer values in [0,num_classes). num_classes is a positive integer excluding booleans.
Return a NumPy array of shape (num_classes,num_classes) containing raw counts, not normalized rates.
Keep rows and columns for absent classes. Repeated outcomes accumulate in their cell.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Each observation adds one to matrix[actual, predicted].

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Use an asymmetric example to detect a transposed matrix.

explanation: A confusion matrix preserves the direction of mistakes: true class a predicted as b is a different outcome from true b predicted as a.
Diagonal entries count correct decisions. Row sums show actual class support, while column sums show how often the model predicts each class.
Inspect a matrix where one rare class is always predicted as a common class. Explain how high overall accuracy can coexist with failure on that rare class.
formula: Cᵢⱼ = count(actual = i and predicted = j)
